skill.name: using-beads-bv
skill.description: Use Beads and bv to plan dependency-aware work, choose ready issues, manage priorities, and record progress through deterministic CLI workflows.
skill.summary: Coordinate dependency-aware task planning with Beads, bv graph insights, ready work selection, and robot-safe CLI workflows.
skill.author: AgentWorkforce

security_audit.summary: The static backtick detections are markdown command examples, not executable Ruby or shell code. The main security concern is the documented session close workflow, which can sync, commit, and push changes without requiring explicit approval.

remediation.issue: Session close workflow can publish changes without approval.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before bd sync, git add, git commit, or git push. Show the planned files and remote before running them.

remediation.issue: Remote synchronization behavior is not clearly bounded.
remediation.suggestion: State that bd sync may contact a remote repository and should only run in trusted workspaces.
Document that bd and bv must be installed from trusted sources before the skill is used.

semantic_findings.title: Unconditional Remote Commit And Push Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The session close protocol tells agents to run bd sync, git add, git commit, and git push before ending a session. Without an explicit approval requirement, this can publish repository changes or task metadata unintentionally.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited workflow explicitly includes remote sync and git push commands. The file does not require user approval before those publishing actions.

content.value_statement: Teams using AI agents need a reliable way to select ready work and avoid dependency conflicts. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Beads and bv workflows for planning, claiming, and closing tasks.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Beads instead of a simple task list.
Lists common bd commands for ready work, task details, creation, updates, and closure.
Shows bv robot flags for graph insights, plans, priorities, recipes, and diffs.
Describes workflows for starting, completing, and creating dependent work.
Defines P0 to P4 priority levels and task identifier conventions.
Reminds agents to use robot flags to avoid interactive blocking.
limitations: Requires bd and bv to be installed and configured in the workspace.
Does not implement the CLI tools or validate their output.
Some commands can change task state or sync data to a remote.
Does not replace project-specific approval, release, or git policies.

use_cases.title: Plan Parallel Agent Work
use_cases.description: Use graph metrics and ready work to assign independent tasks without blocking each other.

use_cases.title: Claim Ready Issues
use_cases.description: Find an unblocked issue, inspect its dependencies, and mark it in progress before coding.

use_cases.title: Maintain Task Traceability
use_cases.description: Use issue identifiers in commits and messages so work can be traced back to Beads tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Find Ready Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me ready Beads work and suggest the next issue to inspect. Use robot-safe commands and do not change task state.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Work Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use bd ready and bv robot planning to build a short execution plan. Identify blockers, parallel tracks, and the safest first task.

prompt_templates.title: Create Dependent Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this feature into Beads tasks with priorities and dependencies. Ask before creating or updating any issue records.

prompt_templates.title: Close A Workstream Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Review completed Beads issues and propose closure steps. Ask before closing issues, syncing, committing, or pushing changes.

output_examples.input: Find the next ready issue for this repository.
output_examples.output: The skill reports ready issues, recommends one starting point, and explains which dependencies make it safe to begin.

output_examples.input: Plan work for a feature and its tests.
output_examples.output: The result separates feature implementation from test work, notes that tests depend on the feature, and suggests suitable priorities.
The skill summarizes closure candidates and asks for approval before syncing, committing, or pushing changes.

best_practices: Confirm bd and bv are installed from trusted sources before using the workflows.
Use bv robot flags so agent sessions receive deterministic output.
Ask before commands that update, close, sync, commit, or push work.
anti_patterns: Using Beads for a small task that only needs a local checklist.
Running the interactive bv interface inside an agent session.
Pushing session changes without reviewing the staged files and remote.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents plan and manage dependency-aware work with Beads and bv.

faq.question: Does it install Beads or bv?
faq.answer: No. The tools must already be installed and configured in the workspace.

faq.question: Can it change project state?
faq.answer: Yes. Some documented commands can update tasks, sync data, commit files, or push changes.

faq.question: Why are robot flags important?
faq.answer: They avoid interactive screens and return output that agents can process reliably.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it for simple single-session work that does not need dependency tracking.

faq.question: Is user approval needed?
faq.answer: Yes. Approval should be required before sync, close, commit, or push operations.
